findings.asked: Equation of the line through two given points.
findings.wentWrong: The strongest found the gradient and the intercept and placed them correctly; a large proportion offered the midpoint instead.
findings.rule: 'Equation of the line' means y = mx + c, not a point.

findings.asked: Equation of a line through two points, one of them on the y-axis.
findings.wentWrong: Gradient was fine; some did not notice the y-intercept was given and went the long way round with substitution, making mistakes.
findings.rule: A point with x = 0 tells you c directly.

findings.asked: Read the intercept, find the gradient and interpret it on a real-life straight-line graph.
findings.wentWrong: The gradient was often given as 1.5 from counting squares without the axis scales. Interpretation needed 'cost per day'; some used scatter-graph language.
findings.rule: Use coordinate values read with the scale, not square counts.

findings.asked: Delivery charge, gradient and meaning on a real-life graph.
findings.wentWrong: Counting squares ignoring the scales gave 23 or 1.5; some divided the two values shown; good candidates who chose awkward points lost accuracy.
findings.rule: Pick two far-apart points on grid intersections and use the scale.

findings.asked: Midpoint, then the equation of the line joining two points.
findings.wentWrong: Mostly full marks; a recurring error put the x-differences on top of the y-differences.
findings.rule: Gradient = change in y over change in x.

findings.asked: Equation of the straight line through two points in the form y = mx + c.
findings.wentWrong: Very limited success: many did a midpoint calculation; only the best used the gradient formula to get -2; diagram approaches missed the negative direction and what the intercept means.
findings.rule: Downhill from left to right means a negative gradient.

findings.asked: Equation of a straight line through two points including (0, 8).
findings.wentWrong: Stronger candidates used the formula and read c = 8 from (0, 8). Weaker ones did rise over run missing the minus, or divided the wrong way round, and few noticed c could be read off.
findings.rule: Check the sign of the gradient and read c from the point on the y-axis.

ruleToRemember: m = (y2 - y1)/(x2 - x1) with coordinates read using the scale; a point on the y-axis gives c; write y = mx + c and check the sign matches the slope.
aStarSignal: Finding and interpreting a gradient on a real-life graph with awkward scales, then writing the equation without prompting.
